title: Short extracts: a chess tournament, hot-desking, a choir concert

segments.speaker: N
segments.text: You hear two chess club members, Emma and Raj, talking about a junior tournament they organised. Emma speaks first.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Well, that's the tournament over for another year, Raj. I'm exhausted.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Me too. But the feedback forms are mostly positive. The parents loved the new café corner.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Did anyone complain about the venue? I know the hall was freezing in the morning.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: One or two did. What surprised me was how many mentioned the timetable. Apparently the gaps between rounds were far too long. The kids were getting restless.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Really? We built those gaps in so that nobody would feel rushed.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I know. But an eight-year-old waiting forty minutes for his next game isn't relaxed. He's bored.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Fair point. So next year we shorten the breaks.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Or we fill them. One parent suggested a puzzle table, where children solve chess problems between games. And it would be cheap.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Cost isn't really the point. But I do prefer it. If we shorten the breaks, we finish an hour earlier, and the parents have all booked their pick-up times.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: True. So puzzles it is. I'll ask Peter to prepare some.

questions.stem: What did a surprising number of parents complain about?

explanation.en: Raj says 'how many mentioned the timetable' and 'the gaps between rounds were far too long'. A is the trap: the cold hall was a complaint, but only 'one or two' parents made it. B is wrong: the parents 'loved the new café corner'.
explanation.cs: Pozor na množství: zimu v sále zmínilo jen 'one or two' rodičů, kdežto 'how many mentioned the timetable' znamená překvapivě mnoho. 'Gaps between rounds' jsou přestávky mezi koly, tedy čekání mezi partiemi.

questions.stem: Why does Emma prefer the puzzle table to shorter breaks?

options.A: It would not change the finishing time.
options.B: It would cost less to organise.
options.C: The children themselves asked for it.

explanation.en: Emma explains that with shorter breaks 'we finish an hour earlier', which clashes with 'pick-up times'. B is Raj's point, and Emma rejects it: 'Cost isn't really the point.' C is wrong: the idea came from 'one parent', not the children.
explanation.cs: Důvod B uvádí Raj a Emma ho výslovně odmítne ('Cost isn't really the point'). Rozhoduje to, že by turnaj skončil o hodinu dřív, než si rodiče naplánovali vyzvednutí dětí. Nápad navrhl jeden z rodičů, ne děti.

segments.speaker: N
segments.text: You hear two colleagues, Clara and Ben, talking about changes to their office. Clara speaks first.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So, Ben. Three weeks of hot-desking. What's the verdict?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I expected to hate it, to be honest. No desk of my own, carrying everything around in a plastic box.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: That part's actually fine. I got used to it much faster than I thought I would. I even quite like sitting next to different people. I've met half the marketing team.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So no complaints at all?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Just one. The noise. When three phone calls are going on around you, it's impossible to write anything properly. I end up taking my laptop home to finish my reports.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Doesn't that defeat the purpose? The whole idea was to bring people together.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Exactly. Management keeps saying it's improved communication. Maybe it has. But not for the work I'm actually paid to do.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Have you told them?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I've drafted an email suggesting a couple of quiet rooms. I'm just not sure it's my place to send it.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Send it. If you don't, nobody will.

questions.stem: How does Ben feel about not having his own desk?

options.B: surprised at how little it bothers him
options.C: pleased that it lets him work from home

explanation.en: Ben 'expected to hate it', but says 'That part's actually fine' and he 'got used to it much faster than I thought'. A was only his expectation. C is wrong: he works at home because of the noise, not because of the desks, and he does not seem pleased about it.
explanation.cs: Past A: 'I expected to hate it' popisuje očekávání, ne skutečný pocit. Slovo 'actually' signalizuje, že realita je jiná, než čekal. Práce z domova je důsledek hluku, ne výhoda sdílených stolů.

questions.stem: What is Clara doing at the end of the conversation?

options.A: encouraging Ben to raise the problem
options.B: advising Ben to speak to management in person
options.C: warning Ben not to criticise management

explanation.en: Ben is unsure whether to send his email, and Clara says 'Send it. If you don't, nobody will.' That is encouragement. B is wrong: she tells him to send the email, not to talk in person. C is the opposite: the doubt about criticising comes from Ben himself ('not sure it's my place').
explanation.cs: Otázka se ptá, co Clara svou poslední replikou dělá (funkce výpovědi). 'Send it' je jasné povzbuzení. Pochybnost 'it's my place' (zda mi to přísluší) vyjadřuje Ben, ne Clara.

segments.speaker: N
segments.text: You hear two friends, Grace and Leo, talking about the choir they sing in. Grace speaks first.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Leo, did you hear? The new director wants us to sing from memory at the spring concert. No sheet music at all.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I heard. Half the basses are threatening to leave.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Are you one of them?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: No. I'm nervous about it, I admit. But I think she's right. When we hold the music, we stare at the page. We never look at her, so we're never quite together.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: That's true. Last year's concert was a bit messy in places.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: And the audience can see our faces properly. It feels more like a performance and less like a rehearsal.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: I'm not convinced it's worth the stress, though. We're volunteers. People join for fun, not to spend every evening learning words.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Well, she's only asking for four pieces by heart. We can still read the music for the rest.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Oh, is that all? Nobody told me that. In that case, I suppose I can manage.

questions.stem: Which reason does Leo give for supporting the director's plan?

options.A: It will help him to overcome his nerves.
options.B: It will make rehearsals more enjoyable.
options.C: It will help the singers to stay in time with each other.

explanation.en: Leo says that with music in their hands 'we never look at her, so we're never quite together'. Singing from memory solves this. A is wrong: he admits he is 'nervous about it', so the plan causes nerves. B is wrong: 'fun' is Grace's word, and it is her argument against the plan.
explanation.cs: 'Never quite together' znamená, že sbor nezpívá přesně spolu, protože se nikdo nedívá na dirigentku. Nervozitu plán naopak vyvolává. Slovo 'fun' použije Grace jako argument proti, ne Leo.

questions.stem: Why does Grace change her mind?

options.A: Leo persuades her that the plan will reduce stress.
options.B: She learns that the task is smaller than she thought.
options.C: She remembers that last year's concert went badly.

explanation.en: When Leo says it is 'only four pieces by heart', Grace replies 'Oh, is that all?' and agrees. A is wrong: Leo never says the plan reduces stress. C is the trap: she mentions the 'messy' concert, but right after that she says 'I'm not convinced', so it does not change her mind.
explanation.cs: Zlom přichází až po informaci 'only four pieces' (jen čtyři skladby zpaměti). 'Is that all?' vyjadřuje úlevu: úkol je menší, než myslela. Zmínka o loňském koncertu je past, protože hned potom ještě nesouhlasí ('I'm not convinced').
